My sorghum plot is small, just under a quarter hectare, and I plant it with cowpea between the rows like my mother taught me. I went to school for a few years so I know fertilizer helps, but one bag of urea is too much for this little plot and costs more cash than I can find after buying food and school things for the children. I will put the goat and chicken droppings I gathered from our compound on the plot, and if my husband gives me some money when the agro-dealer brings the subsidy fertilizer, I will buy a small share of a bag with my neighbor and sprinkle a little urea when the sorghum is knee-high. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest because the local kind does well here and I cannot waste money on hybrid seed for sorghum — nobody in my village buys sorghum seed.
